clues: The neighbor who drew the owl label made more cider than the one who drew the moon.
Of the neighbor who made 5 gallons and the one who made 10, one pressed the wild mix and the other the tart.
The tart and spicy mixes came from two different neighbors: one made 5 gallons, the other 15 gallons.
Cyrus made more cider than Felix.
Whoever drew the star label made exactly 5 gallons more than whoever pressed the spicy mix.
Marta made less cider than the neighbor who drew the moon.
Felix made exactly 5 gallons more than the neighbor with the moon label.
hints: Look at the 5-gallon row in the box where labels meet gallons. Which label could possibly belong to the smallest batch?
Comparisons rule out the ends: clue 1 keeps the owl off 5 gallons. What do clues 5 and 6 say about the star and the moon?
So the anchor made 5 gallons. The moon made 10 or 15, so by clues 7 and 4, Felix made 15 and the moon 10.
The star made 15 or 20, so by clue 5 the spicy mix made 10 or 15. Clue 2 rules out 10.

solution.key_idea: Clues 1, 5 and 6 keep the owl, star and moon labels off 5 gallons, so the anchor went on the smallest batch.
steps: Clue 1 keeps the owl off 5 gallons, clue 5 the star, and clue 6 the moon. So the anchor label made 5 gallons.
The moon made neither 5 (clue 6) nor 20 (clue 1). By clue 7, Felix made 5 more than the moon, so 15 or 20.
Clue 4 keeps Felix off 20, so Felix made 15 and the moon 10. Cyrus, above Felix, made 20.
By clue 6, Marta made less than 10, so 5 gallons, with the anchor. Priya made 10, with the moon.
The star made 15 or 20, so by clue 5 the spicy mix made 10 or 15. Clue 2 rules out 10, leaving Felix's 15.
So by clue 5 the star made 20: Cyrus drew it. Felix, with 15, drew the owl.
By clue 3, the tart made 5 gallons: Marta's. By clue 2, Priya's 10 gallons were wild, and Cyrus pressed the sweet.
solution.epilogue: Fifty gallons in all: Cyrus's sweet under a star, Felix's spicy under an owl, Priya's wild under a moon and Marta's tart under an anchor. Felix took his fair share.
